subject: System Design
title: Packets and Routers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Packets and Routers usable.

hook.text: When you send a message online, it doesn't travel as one piece. It's split into tiny packets.

buildup.text: Each packet carries a piece of data, a source address, and a destination address.

discovery.text: Routers read destination addresses and forward packets hop by hop across networks until they arrive.

twist.text: Packets from the same message can take different routes and arrive out of order. The receiver reassembles them.

climax.text: Packet switching is the internet's foundation. No single path is dedicated — networks share bandwidth.

punchline.text: The internet splits data into packets and routes them independently.

quiz.question: How do packets travel across the internet?
options: Routers forward them hop by hop based on destination addresses
They travel in a single dedicated path
